release_critical_followups.head: 74bb9fa84b85a9bf1f58f89e5d35762f728ed17b
release_critical_followups.status: open draft at review; no merge performed
release_critical_followups.action: Root should include verified extreme-query, integer-overflow, Python allocation and duplicate persisted-ID fixes in the release candidate, run required integrated gates, and retain the sealed-snapshot boundary limits.

evidence.head: 74bb9fa84b85a9bf1f58f89e5d35762f728ed17b
evidence.statement:
Finite extreme cosine queries could return reversed rankings; large supported dimensions could overflow integer dot products; huge or empty padded Python results could abort; and duplicate persisted IDs could load as valid. This change fixes those boundaries with independent regression oracles and preserves ordinary-query results.

It also pairs primary/residual reranking loads, bounds prefetch distance, and adds explicit Linux sealed-snapshot loading so worker processes can share immutable index pages. Private heap loading remains the default. A publisher helper records setup cost and binds the exact sealed inode; ordinary mutable files and insufficient seals are rejected.

Local full VectorDBBench runs show modest throughput gains and a separate memory tradeoff. The combined kernel/prefetch arm averaged 4.94% above main in the first interleaved ablation. A later released-wheel comparison retained negative results, including a faster grouped released wheel. On 8 logical CPUs with a 16 GiB limit, sharing reduced mean peak cgroup memory 77.34% (14.21 to 3.22 GiB) while reducing mean maximum QPS 2.70%, at unchanged recall@100=.9406. It is not enabled by default or presented as a throughput win.

Validation: default Rust 1,018 passed, all-features 1,667 passed; fmt, clippy default/python/all-features and MSRV 1.89 passed. Linux Python 164 passed with 3 feature skips; Mac 131 passed with 36 Linux-only skips. Snapshot binding tests: 24 passed. Full ordered-ID replay matches at six search efforts; component ablations and rejected alternatives are retained.

The [evidence report](https://github.com/writerslogic/warm/blob/perf/vdbbench-low-level/docs/research/LOWLEVEL-SYSTEMS.md#static-graph-follow-up-2026-11-09) and raw results are committed. At the user's stop request, the frozen Azure VectorDBBench package had passed input verification and image loading, but its first workload had not started. The service was stopped; no Azure VectorDBBench number is claimed. The draft retains the frozen package and an explicit stop receipt for future continuation. All development uses owned hosts. No query-quality setting was selected from the new full-set measurements, and previously exposed public queries are not described as an untouched holdout. These source changes are unreleased; VectorDBBench PR 898 remains pinned to published warm-python 0.6.4.

Independent frozen ANN confirmation is also recorded: Azure E8bds_v5 streaming E2a reached .9965711875 recall in both full runs (2865.57/2871.94 seconds, below the preregistered 3240-second gate); the submitted filter configuration reached 54721.70/53972.75 QPS at .906415 recall. Those runs use their own older frozen pins and are not measurements of this PR's new source. E8bds_v5 is not the official D8lds_v5 platform; no official rank is claimed.

source_pr_snapshots.head: 4a54fc75223872f3e62dd263231a2a0903247866
source_pr_snapshots.statement:
Lands the finished parts of issues #1, #42 and #163 plus two comparator/as_of levers. Negative or parked work (#4, #164, #165, postings block size, supersession probe) stays on branches and is not in this PR.

## Included
- **#1 AVX2 screen popcount** (`src/core/qgraph/kernels.rs`): 1.05x to 1.75x over POPCNT for 4 or more words on this machine, paired ratios only. AVX-512 is not wired or verified. The issue's 4x to 10x target is not met, so the issue stays open.
- **#42 background compaction** (`src/core/engine/background_compaction.rs`, Node `startCompaction`, design in `docs/file-format/COMPACTION.md`): bounded worker with progress, cancel and budgets; foreground reads and writes continue. `index.d.ts` regenerated. Release latency run not done.
- **#163 time-travel views** (`src/core/engine/history.rs`, `docs/memory-api/TIME-TRAVEL.md`): read-only historical view, opt-in. `tests/time_travel.rs` compares every earlier position to a fresh store. Cost: opening a view per query is 813x (1k docs) to 4,246x (10k docs) a live search; a view kept open is 0.65x to 0.89x (`benchmarks/results/history_view_cost.json`). HTTP and SDK not done.
- **as_of overfetch** (`docs/research/as-of-overfetch.md`): no library change. The API already filters before top-k, so overfetch is a no-go. Records that the committed 14-hit memory_api result reproduces as 13 at its own commit.
- **Comparator re-pin** (tantivy 0.27.0, Lucene 10.6.0, SQLite 3.53.1, previous-pin controls): no throughput or latency class flips in the local paired run. The published tables are unchanged; `table.py` now labels Lucene with the version each result file recorded instead of the current pin. Modal results are still Lucene 9.12.3 and `GAPS.json` is not regenerated against the new pins.

## Verified locally
`cargo fmt -- --check`; `cargo +1.99.0 clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and default features; same clippy with `--target x86_64-apple-darwin`; `cargo test`; `cargo test --all-features`; `cargo +1.89.0 check --locked --no-default-features`; `scripts/check-generated.sh`; `check-versions.py`; `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:types` (macOS arm64 only).

## Not verified
Linux and Windows Node jobs, AVX-512, and the other CI jobs run here for the first time.

source_pr_snapshots.head: e2a00f488640e470f910d995d15072344a412ae8
source_pr_snapshots.statement:
## What

Four independently developed pieces, merged without conflicts:

- **Per-store lexical analyzers** (`lever/language-analyzers`). `WarmConfig::analyzer` is recorded in `store.json` as `lexical_analyzer` and marked on chunks with flag bit 7 plus a matching checkpoint bit. Stores without the key keep the legacy analysis byte for byte; older releases refuse marked stores; replay refuses a chunk whose mark disagrees with `store.json`. Adds per-language Snowball selection, Persian and Hindi normalization with light stemming, Thai/CJK character bigrams, NFC and Turkish dotted/dotless I folding (non-legacy analyzers only). MIRACL dev nDCG@10 and a comparator against Lucene 10.6.0 language analyzers are in `benchmarks/results/multilingual_bm25_analyzers_miracl_dev.json`; the default analyzer reproduces the previous top-100 ids and scores on every query, including SciFact, NFCorpus and LongMemEval. A store written by a090f971 is committed as `tests/fixtures/legacy-analyzer-store` and must reopen with identical rankings and scores.
- **Historical view open cost** (`lever/view-open`). Views are bulk-indexed once instead of frame by frame. 10k docs, paired factor vs the previous build: 8.12x cheaper at the latest position, 3.2x at the middle (1k docs: 5.26x, 1.89x). The reuse cache is off by default and opt-in via `set_history_cache_budget`, because it retains index memory after callers drop views. No format change.
- **Deterministic simulation harness** (`lever/sim-harness`). `tests/simulation.rs` drives seeded operation sequences against a naive bitemporal model across writes, supersession, forget, compaction, purge, reopen and a crash copy, checking search, status at as_of/known_at, history positions and a multiset hash. 200 seeds by default; no library bugs found.
- **Counting-Bloom erratum** (`lever/bloom-equal-bits`). The documented 4x capacity of the counting readout came from k = 64 and from unequal bits. With tuned k a binary Bloom filter at the same dimension matches it to 4000 items, and at equal bits it scores AUC 1.000. Docs and the module comment are corrected; script and result are committed.

## Not done / follow-ups

Node, Python and WASM bindings for the analyzer setting, `warm-admin reencode` carrying the analyzer, the reused-view damage check, stop words, and view-open still short of a 10x target on a cold open.

## Gates

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo +1.99.0 clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo test --all-features`, `cargo deny check licenses` and the generated-files check all exit 0 on this branch.

source_pr_snapshots.head: f59bad25d433b44bfc3dcf47921508bab25d4636
source_pr_snapshots.statement:
Refreshes the competitive text comparison at pinned source revisions and lands a measured serving speedup.

**Benchmarks**
- Core Ultra 9 standard text rows rerun at `4b7a849f`. The previous rows had an unpinned source revision, so every verdict read n/v.
- Modal heavy text rows rerun at `7ba2d4fe`, which has the same engine source as `4b7a849f`. The comparators are tantivy 0.27, Lucene 10.6 and SQLite 3.53.1.
- The Modal image now installs a sha256-pinned Temurin 21. Debian bookworm has no JDK 21, and Lucene 10 needs it.
- Results on SciFact, NFCorpus and memory, on both machines:
  - 6 wins, 2 ties and 2 losses each.
  - 1.66x to 2.00x the single-thread QPS of the best comparator.
  - 1.69x to 2.91x less serving RSS and 3.1x to 5.7x faster cold start.
  - nDCG@10 ties.
- Losses:
  - FiQA QPS is 0.78x of Lucene 10.6.
  - Build peak RSS and ingest time trail SQLite FTS5.
- The README rows now name the machine they were measured on. The ingest, build-RSS and QPS lever notes state what was profiled.

**Serving**
- `Postings::for_each` decodes one- and two-byte words and frequencies from the loaded 64-bit word.
- Paired on M4 over 6 interleaved rounds, with identical results:
  - FiQA 1.092x
  - SciFact 1.014x
  - NFCorpus 1.005x
  - memory 1.002x
- A new test checks that decoding matches the checked decoder at every varint length boundary and window offset.

Merge with a merge commit. The Modal result files cite `7ba2d4fe`.
